question: Alcohol-based hand rub (ABHR) is effective for hand decontamination after caring for a patient with Clostridioides difficile infection.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: C. difficile spores are resistant to alcohol-based hand rubs. Mechanical removal with soap and water (40–60 seconds) is mandatory for CDI. ABHR remains the preferred method for routine hand hygiene in all other clinical situations where hands are not visibly soiled.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. C. difficile produces spores that are resistant to alcohol. Soap and water with physical friction for 40–60 seconds is mandatory after CDI contact. ABHR is preferred for most other pathogens because it is faster and more effective against non-spore-forming transient flora.
